title: Trading workflows, venues and counterparties
objectives: Trace an instruction through broker/venue/execution/post-trade roles while distinguishing order acknowledgment, fills, cancel confirmation and settlement.
Compare stated venue/execution alternatives on price, size, cost, latency and uncertainty without mistaking a quote or toy snapshot for guaranteed executable liquidity.
Apply trading workflows, venues and counterparties invariants safely and identify scope boundaries.
motivation: This module teaches market mechanics using synthetic single-currency stock/share examples, not a recommendation to trade or a claim about the user's broker. Sources include US securities-market education; specific legal obligations, permitted order types, tax/settlement cycles and access rules vary by jurisdiction, asset, venue and account.

blocks.md: This module teaches market mechanics using synthetic single-currency stock/share examples, not a recommendation to trade or a claim about the user's broker. Sources include US securities-market education; specific legal obligations, permitted order types, tax/settlement cycles and access rules vary by jurisdiction, asset, venue and account. Do not apply a US example as an Indian or worldwide rule. Every real transaction needs its own current instrument/account/venue contract and authorization.

An investor or fund sends an instruction. A broker acts for a customer in arranging/executing a transaction; a dealer trades for its own account as principal. The same firm can perform both roles on different transactions, so identify capacity rather than inferring it from the brand. A market maker quotes buying/selling interest under its applicable arrangements and bears inventory/adverse-selection risk; earning a quoted spread is not a guaranteed profit. A venue is a place/system for trading under its rules, not automatically the customer's broker, custodian or legal counterparty.

Execution establishes a trade's price/quantity under its contract; clearing determines/processes obligations and may net/guarantee eligible trades; settlement transfers the required cash/securities through the applicable infrastructure. Custody/recordkeeping concerns holding assets and recording entitlements. In eligible centrally cleared systems, a clearing counterparty can interpose through novation, subject to acceptance/rules. This is not how every asset/OTC trade clears, and it does not remove all liquidity, operational, legal or default risk. DTCC's CNS is a concrete US service example, not a universal workflow.

blocks.title: Do not collapse different confirmations into one success flag
items: A customer submits a request to buy 100 shares through a broker. Local send success records transmission, not venue acceptance or a trade.
The venue accepts the order. That acknowledgment may establish an order identifier/open quantity under the venue protocol, but no fill has occurred yet.

A confirmed execution for 30 shares leaves 70 open. The customer asks to cancel the remainder; before that request is processed, another 20 shares may execute. The cancel confirmation can then remove only 50 remaining shares.

The cumulative confirmed state is filled 50, canceled 50, open 0. The request to cancel 70 did not undo the extra 20 filled before cancellation. Trade obligations still need the applicable post-trade processing/settlement; a canceled remainder is not a reversal of existing trades.

blocks.caption: Expected dictionaries: {'filled': 0, 'canceled': 0, 'open': 100}; {'filled': 30, 'canceled': 0, 'open': 70}; {'filled': 50, 'canceled': 50, 'open': 0}; then inconsistent state rejected. The fixed requested quantity satisfies requested=filled+canceled+open. This helper checks a declared cumulative snapshot only; it does not authenticate events, detect duplicates/replaces/corrections or implement a broker protocol/state machine.

blocks.md: A displayed limit-order book exposes some priced interest and matches under a rulebook; an auction collects interest for a defined matching event; a dealer/request-for-quote interaction seeks a quoted trade from a counterparty. Listed instruments can trade through routes beyond one listing venue, and OTC does not mean one universal execution mechanism. These models can differ in transparency, liquidity, price formation, timing, size, access and counterparty/clearing arrangements. Do not label one globally best from a venue name alone.

Compare the same instrument, side, currency, settlement basis, order size and timestamp context. For a BUY, raw lower price is better all else equal, but fees and executable size matter. Quotes are for particular quantities and can change before arrival. Evaluate all-in expected cost, chance/size of fill, latency, information leakage, adverse selection and operational reliability under the strategy's constraints. A fee rebate alone or the fastest acknowledgment alone does not establish best execution or lowest total economic cost.

blocks.caption: Expected output: A (10050, Fraction(1005, 1)); B (10010, Fraction(1001, 1)); C None. Buying 10 shares at A costs 10000 cents plus 50 fee; B costs 10010 with no fee. Thus B is lower cost in this exact frozen full-fill fixture despite its worse quoted per-share price. C cannot fill the whole 10 at its displayed size 5 under the helper's no-splitting policy. No route is selected for a real order; changes/partial fills/hidden interest/cross-venue routing are excluded.

blocks.md: Keep client request IDs, broker/venue order IDs and execution IDs separate; their namespace/mapping comes from the protocol. The same-looking identifier from another account/venue need not be the same event. Event/exchange timestamp, receipt timestamp and processing sequence can differ. A missing or delayed response is not proof an order failed and safe to resubmit. Later modules implement sequence/idempotency state; here record uncertainty and reconcile authoritative reports instead of inventing a fill or duplicate order.

Track confirmed executions and open exposure separately. An unfilled order may still create future execution risk until cancellation is effective; settlement obligations can remain after the order is fully filled/canceled. Fees, settlement calendars, margin/short-sale rules, corporate actions, counterparty and legal terms require their actual current sources. This module deliberately does not teach a universal settlement day count, promise trade finality from an acknowledgment, or authorize a live order.

Independent transfer: annotate a timeline containing send, acknowledgment, partial fill, cancel request, another fill, cancel confirmation and settlement evidence. At each point state what is known and what remains uncertain, and reconcile share counts. Then compare two synthetic buy quotes including fees and limited displayed size. Name facts still missing before turning that comparison into an executable routing choice.

References: [SEC investor trade execution](https://www.investor.gov/introduction-investing/investing-basics/how-stock-markets-work/executing-order), [FINRA broker/dealer roles](https://www.finra.org/investors/investing/working-with-investment-professional/registered-financial-professionals), [confirmation capacity/fees](https://www.finra.org/investors/insights/checking-trade-confirmations), and [DTCC CNS eligible clearing/novation/settlement](https://www.dtcc.com/products-and-services/clearing-settlement-services/equities-clearing/cns). US-specific examples are labeled, synthetic policies are not venue facts, and no brokerage capability is assumed.

guidedExercise.prompt: A trade is marked filled by one report but absent from a local ledger. What would you check before retrying the order?
hints: Preserves identity and confirmed execution evidence.
Checks reconciliation/recovery rather than blind retry.
guidedExercise.solution: Check account/instrument/order/execution identities, authoritative reports and cumulative fills, message sequence/duplicates/corrections and local commit/recovery status. Treat the outcome as uncertain; do not infer failure and duplicate the order.

independentExercise.prompt: Write a small test case that deliberately breaks the contract boundary in "Trading workflows, venues and counterparties" and verify how your implementation rejects or handles it.
hints: Test zero, negative, empty, duplicate, and boundary values.
Confirm both time/memory complexity and numerical precision remain within spec.

commonMistakes: The example explicitly separates acceptance from later execution and post-trade events. (No execution has occurred yet in the stated sequence.)
Only the unfilled remainder can be canceled in this synthetic sequence. (Cumulative fill 50 plus cancellation 50 leaves open 0.)
In the frozen fixture, B's one-cent worse quote is outweighed by A's 50 cent fee on 10 shares. (Compare matched quantity/currency and complete fee assumptions.)
realWorldApplication: Used directly across production quantitative research, execution systems, and validation pipelines.
quantFinanceApplication: Applies rigorous engineering contracts to quantitative modeling and live trading infrastructure.
summary: Order send, acceptance, execution, cancellation and settlement are distinct.
Identify transaction roles/capacity and reconcile confirmed exposure; compare routes under explicit size/cost/time assumptions rather than assuming a quote or acknowledgment guarantees a fill.
Trace an instruction through broker/venue/execution/post-trade roles while distinguishing order acknowledgment, fills, cancel confirmation and settlement.

quiz.prompt: What does an order acknowledgment establish in the stated example?
options: All requested shares are already settled
The venue has accepted the order under its protocol
A cancel request can undo all later fills
The broker is always the final clearing counterparty
quiz.explanation: The example explicitly separates acceptance from later execution and post-trade events. (No execution has occurred yet in the stated sequence.)

quiz.prompt: An order has filled 30 of 100 shares. After a cancel request, 20 more fill before cancel confirmation. How much can the final cancel remove if nothing else happens?
options: Zero because partial fills always disable cancellation
quiz.explanation: Only the unfilled remainder can be canceled in this synthetic sequence. (Cumulative fill 50 plus cancellation 50 leaves open 0.)

quiz.prompt: Why can a slightly higher quoted buy price have lower all-in cost?
options: Its explicit fee can be sufficiently lower
A per-order fee can be ignored whenever the per-share quote is lower
A better quoted price always offsets any fixed fee at every order size
quiz.explanation: In the frozen fixture, B's one-cent worse quote is outweighed by A's 50 cent fee on 10 shares. (Compare matched quantity/currency and complete fee assumptions.)

quiz.prompt: What remains uncertain after observing a displayed quote?
options: The snapshot has no usable information at all
Every requested size will execute at that price
The quote is necessarily a completed trade
Its availability when the order arrives
quiz.explanation: A visible quote is not a reservation or a guarantee of the user's execution. (Delay, competing flow and changes can alter accessible liquidity.)

quiz.prompt: Requested 100, confirmed filled 50, canceled 50. What is open quantity under the stated invariant?
quiz.explanation: 100=50+50+0. Counting requested cancellation 70 would overcount after the extra 20 fill.
